Planning outcome for 5271

Scope: produce and validate the compaction design; do not implement production compaction or rewrite refs/work/knots history.

1. Add deterministic Node 20 tooling: scripts/event-log-fixture.mjs creates 50,000 full and 30,000 index files across 40 dated buckets; scripts/event-log-inventory.mjs reports full/index/snapshot/manifest counts, bytes, daily rate, and five-run median no-op scan timing as stable JSON. Add small node:test coverage and a Make target for reproducibility.
2. Run the 80k fixture and record the measured result and machine/filesystem context in docs/event-log-compaction.md. Define the post-compaction target as 2,003 JSON files (2,000 retained events, two snapshots, one manifest), median no-op time <=1,000 ms and <=25% of baseline.
3. Trace src/replication.rs, src/snapshots.rs, src/sync/apply.rs, and src/sync/apply_quarantine.rs. Explain the O(total retained history) scan/byte comparison, snapshot v1 pairing/atomicity gaps, Git-SHA watermarks, quarantine bases, and stale-store resurrection.
4. Specify protocol v2: an immutable checkpoint manifest binds generation, cutoff commit, active/cold snapshot hashes and counts, retained paths, compatibility floor, and state. Publish PREPARED checkpoint artifacts while history remains, then CAS-activate and prune only paths proven in the cutoff tree. Preserve all post-cutoff and unique unpushed events. Local pruning occurs only after observing ACTIVE.
5. Make mixed-version safety explicit. A client-only manifest is insufficient because legacy writers ignore it. Freeze the legacy replication namespace and activate a generation-two namespace protected by the hosting push rail; unsupported writers fail before staging. No permanently online coordinator is needed.
6. Specify transactional checkpoint reconciliation for fresh bootstrap, pre-cutoff watermarks, and leased/quarantined knots. Hash/schema failure leaves watermarks and quarantine unchanged. Recovery ignores PREPARED/orphan artifacts; rollback selects a prior complete generation while Git ancestry remains.
7. Add an executable protocol-model test covering bootstrap, pre-cutoff watermark, lease quarantine, stale writer, concurrent writer, interrupted publication before/after activation, mixed-version rejection, rollback, and no-op second sync. Keep the 80k run opt-in; make sanity runs the small deterministic fixture and safety oracle.
8. Finish docs with the recommendation not to rewrite Git history initially. Deletion commits bound HEAD scan cost but retain old Git objects. A later rewrite/GC would shrink repository storage but invalidate watermarks and quarantine bases and requires a separate coordinated migration.
9. Run the checked-in benchmark, targeted tests, size checks, and make sanity. Review the report against every acceptance criterion.

Follow-on implementation knots (related, not parent/child, so this design knot can ship independently):
- 5807 rank 1, effort 1: manifest/checkpoint schema and protocol model.
- 5728 rank 2, effort 2, blocked by 5807: generation-two push fence, publisher, and local pruner.
- 2af8 rank 2, effort 2, blocked by 5807: checkpoint-aware bootstrap, watermarks, and quarantine.
- 246b rank 3, effort 1, blocked by 5728 and 2af8: Quilt-scale fixture, end-to-end verification, and rollout.

Aggregate implementation estimate remains effort 4, not the arithmetic sum of leaf tags: ranks 2 run in parallel, share the schema/model, and the final verification leaf is integration work. Principal risks are hosting support for freezing the legacy namespace, transactional lease reconciliation, cutoff ordering under concurrent writers, snapshot size under blob filtering, and the fact that HEAD retention does not reclaim historical Git objects.
